headline: Country music legend Dolly Parton dies at 80
summary: The Grammy-winning singer and songwriter, known for hits like 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You', has passed away.
details: Dolly Parton, the iconic country music singer, songwriter, and actress, died on Tuesday at the age of 80. Her family confirmed the news in a statement, marking the end of a career that spanned nearly six decades.
Born into a 'dirt-poor' family in Tennessee as one of 12 children, Parton rose from humble beginnings to become one of the best-selling female artists of all time, selling over 100 million records.
She won 11 Grammy awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award, and penned timeless classics such as 'Coat of Many Colors,' 'Jolene,' and 'I Will Always Love You.'
Beyond music, Parton was a successful businesswoman and actress, creating the popular Dollywood theme park in her home state of Tennessee and starring in various films.
Parton was widely respected for her philanthropy, donating $1 million to Vanderbilt University for Covid-19 vaccine research and establishing literacy programs for preschool children globally.
Her ability to connect with people across political divides in a polarized America was a hallmark of her career, fueled by her nonpartisanship and commitment to her roots.
caption:
From a one-room cabin to global superstardom. Dolly Parton, the queen of country music, has passed away at 80.

Dolly Parton, the iconic country music singer, songwriter, and actress, died on Tuesday at the age of 80. Her family confirmed the news in a statement, marking the end of a career that spanned nearly six decades.

Born into a 'dirt-poor' family in Tennessee as one of 12 children, Parton rose from humble beginnings to become one of the best-selling female artists of all time, selling over 100 million records.

She won 11 Grammy awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award, and penned timeless classics such as 'Coat of Many Colors,' 'Jolene,' and 'I Will Always Love You.'

Beyond music, Parton was a successful businesswoman and actress, creating the popular Dollywood theme park in her home state of Tennessee and starring in various films.

Parton was widely respected for her philanthropy, donating $1 million to Vanderbilt University for Covid-19 vaccine research and establishing literacy programs for preschool children globally.

Her ability to connect with people across political divides in a polarized America was a hallmark of her career, fueled by her nonpartisanship and commitment to her roots.

headline_marked: 14 children killed in [[hospital fire in Pakistan's capital]]
headline: 14 children killed in hospital fire in Pakistan's capital
summary: A fire broke out in the maternity ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, claiming the lives of 14 children.
details: A fire erupted in a maternity ward in Islamabad on Wednesday, killing 14 children, according to the Islamabad district office.
The blaze broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Health Ward at the public Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital.
Emergency calls were made just before 7:00 am, prompting rescue teams, specialists, and police to respond to the site to control the fire.
Islamabad chief commissioner Sohail Ashraf confirmed the response and stated that the rescue operations were managed immediately.
The incident highlights a recurring issue in Pakistan, where fires in large buildings are frequent due to poor safety laws and building codes.
Past tragedies include a shopping center fire in Karachi in January that killed over 65 people, and another shopping mall fire in 2023 that killed 11.
Other significant losses occurred in factory fires in Karachi in 2021 and 2012, including the Baldia Town garment factory fire that killed at least 250 laborers.
caption:
14 children lost their lives in a devastating hospital fire in Islamabad.

A fire erupted in a maternity ward in Islamabad on Wednesday, killing 14 children, according to the Islamabad district office.

The blaze broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Health Ward at the public Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital.

Emergency calls were made just before 7:00 am, prompting rescue teams, specialists, and police to respond to the site to control the fire.

Islamabad chief commissioner Sohail Ashraf confirmed the response and stated that the rescue operations were managed immediately.

The incident highlights a recurring issue in Pakistan, where fires in large buildings are frequent due to poor safety laws and building codes.

Past tragedies include a shopping center fire in Karachi in January that killed over 65 people, and another shopping mall fire in 2023 that killed 11.

Other significant losses occurred in factory fires in Karachi in 2021 and 2012, including the Baldia Town garment factory fire that killed at least 250 laborers.
